db_conflicts.research_value: "3*5 cm." as literally published by the Royal Thai Embassy, Brussels (read as 3cm × 5cm)

cross_verification.note_en: Thailand's e-Passport is a biometric document, and multiple official Royal Thai missions state the photo is captured live at the appointment rather than submitted by the applicant. The Royal Thai Embassy Washington DC's passport-renewal FAQ states verbatim: "No, you do not need to [bring a photo]. The officer will take your photo on the day of your appointment." (https://washingtondc.thaiembassy.org/en/page/faqspprenewal). The Royal Thai Embassy Seoul's Thai National Passport requirements page (https://seoul.thaiembassy.org/en/publicservice/thai-national-passport) lists only ID/passport/residence documents among requirements and describes in-person "biometric data collection, such as fingerprinting, photography, and iris scanning" — again no self-submitted photo. Against this, the Royal Thai Embassy Brussels page used above for the verified fields DOES list a photograph ("3*5 cm., white background") among required documents for its passport application. These official sources are not fully reconcilable from public pages alone — it is possible Brussels still wants a printed photo attached to the paper form even though the actual passport image is captured biometrically on-site, or requirements differ slightly by mission. The size/background figures above should be read as confirmed for the Brussels mission specifically, not as a universal Thai passport photo standard.
